This report is part of Objective 3, and it synthesizes the research performed by the authors and focuses on aspects of collocation of OTEC with floating oil and gas facilities in the GOA. It presents the modeled case for integrating OTEC with a floating oil and gas facility for potential offset of the host facility’s power demand. Specifically, the case study in this report focuses on presenting the structural challenges and limitations of coupling OTEC systems with existing or projected facility designs. Separately, the case study of monitoring for methane emissions, which is also part of Objective 3 activities, is documented in a paper and presentation showcased in the 2025 Offshore Technology Conference (Grelle, et al. 2025). The deliverables for Objective 1 and 2 (i.e., Volumes 1 and 2) will be referred to as “Objective 1 report” or “Objective 2 report” throughout this report. 2 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 3 Objectives In the Objective 1 report, the analysis of well methane emissions monitoring systems is documented. They included continuous monitoring solutions, such as battery powered passive acoustic and chemical sensors, as well as periodic monitoring with ROV and AUVs. In the Objective 2 phase of the study, a numerical OTEC model was developed to determine the net power output of an OTEC plant in different locations in the GOA as a function of marine resources such as water depth and water column temperature gradient, as well as available components comprising an OTEC plant, such as heat exchangers, working fluids, cold- and warm-water intake pipes of varying sizes, and so on. In this report, which corresponds to Objective 3 of the study, a collocation scheme is presented whereby OTEC can integrate with an oil and gas facility and provide power to the facility itself as well as power monitoring of wells located some distance from the facility. For the purposes of this study—and given the fact that primarily deepwater areas in the GOA (i.e., deeper than 1,000 ft) are able to accommodate OTEC requirements—the type of facility considered is a floating production platform. Furthermore, a generic semi- submersible platform design was selected due to the noted trend of this type of design being deployed in the deeper waters of the GOA. There are two main outputs of this study. First, findings are presented with respect to the possibilities and challenges in integrating an OTEC plant with a floating facility such as a semi-submersible platform. Additionally, a simplified interactive map is presented that aims to aid the general public in understanding the hypothetical possibilities for OTEC deployment in the Gulf of America (GOA) taking into account GOA’s marine resources as well as OTEC component availability in the current market. 4 Locating an OTEC Plant OTEC was selected to be examined as part of this study because of its ability to provide power continuously to facilities and operations in the GOA as documented
